abstract_research_topics.justification: Convex optimization is a fundamental mathematical theory that focuses on the optimization of convex functions, which is a purely abstract research topic involving rigorous mathematical proofs and concepts.

Non-convex optimization is concerned with understanding and finding optimal solutions in non-convex problem spaces. This is primarily a theoretical domain as it involves extensive mathematics and theoretical understanding to tackle these problems.
This involves the theoretical study of optimization within function spaces, focusing on mathematical properties and abstract reasoning rather than specific applications.
Discrete optimization is a theoretical domain within operations research and mathematics dealing with optimization in discrete spaces and involves significant abstract research.
This involves finding optimal solutions in continuous domains, which is largely theoretical and involves mathematical formulations and algorithms.

application_domains.justification: This domain focuses on practical methods and techniques where optimization is done offline, specifically in application scenarios like automated design or industry.
As a direct application of optimization methods, this domain deals with the design process in engineering and manufacturing, requiring practical implementation of optimization techniques.
Model optimization is a procedure practically documented within machine learning and deep learning to improve model performance and efficiency in real-world tasks.
This domain focuses on applying models to solve optimization problems within specific contexts, hence it is application-oriented.
This involves adaptable methods in optimization to be employed in varied, real-world scenarios, emphasizing practical application.
